title: 2.5 A 16nm 5.7TOPS CNN Processor Supporting Bi-Directional FPN for Small-Object Detection on High-Resolution Videos
problem: Small-object detection in high-resolution (2M-pixel) images requires deep networks (77-layer backbones) with multi-scale feature extraction, but high memory bandwidth and compute requirements limit deployment in energy-constrained and mobile scenarios.
motivation: Autonomous vehicles, drones, VR/AR, and robots demand efficient detection of distant/small pedestrians and objects (<1K pixels in 2M images) for safety-critical ADAS systems.
method: 16nm CNN processor combining orientation-interleaved-causally-processed (OICP) modeling for bi-FPN feature-map memory reduction, bandwidth-optimized backbone scheduling (RARC re-access/re-compute), and reconfigurable tensor engine (RTE) supporting diverse operations, achieving 5.7TOPS throughput.
key_novelty: OICP bi-FPN and RARC backbone scheduling co-optimized to reduce external-memory-access for high-resolution multi-scale feature processing.
contributions: 5.7TOPS for deep CNN backbones (77-layer EfficientDet-D3) on high-resolution (896x896) inputs
OICP bi-FPN reducing feature-map memory footprint without mAP loss
Reconfigurable tensor engine supporting diverse operations (convolution, pooling, non-linearities) for improved utilization
baselines: prior CNN accelerators for object detection
limitations: Energy efficiency, latency, and detailed mAP results on COCO dataset not provided in abstract.
